target.title: feat: reproduce and attest declared real behavior proof (issue 421, scope 1)
target.body:
## Summary

Implements scope 1 of https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/issues/421: ClawSweeper can now reproduce a PR's declared real behavior proof instead of only reading it, and record the result as a head-SHA-pinned attestation.

Today proof is a single model judgment: the review model emits `RealBehaviorProof`, deterministic code turns `status: "sufficient"` into the `proof: sufficient` label, and nothing ever re-runs the claimed reproduction (`grep -rn "attest" src/` on main returns nothing). This PR adds the reproducible half of that trust chain:

- `realBehaviorProof.reproCommand` (string or null): a new schema field the review model fills with the single deterministic offline command the PR evidence names, only for `terminal`, `logs`, or `live_output` evidence, and null in every other case.
- A reproduction engine (`src/reproduce-proof.ts`) that runs the declared command on base twice and head once inside a network-denied, credential-free sandbox that always executes as a non-root identity (`sudo -n unshare --net -- setpriv --reuid=... --regid=... --clear-groups -- env -i ...`), and decides on exit codes and output hashes only.
- An attestation record (`src/proof-attestation.ts` plus `schema/clawsweeper-proof-attestation.schema.json`) written to `records/<slug>/proof/<number>.json`. Readers recompute `stable`, `differentiates`, and `verdict` from the run fields; nothing trusts those values from disk.
- A `reproduce-proof` subcommand (lane) that scans reviewed PR reports, checks eligibility (open, non-draft PR with a declared command, reproducible evidence kind, live head matching the reviewed head), runs the engine, writes the record, and upserts one head-SHA-keyed marker comment beside the model verdict.

The verdict is `attested` only when the two base runs match exactly and the head run differs by exit code or output hash. Every failure mode is `neutral`, never attested: `netns_unavailable`, `command_unresolvable`, `checkout_failed`, `sandbox_access_failed`, `setup_failed`, `timeout`, `run_failed`, `flaky_base`, `no_delta`. Running base twice rejects reproductions that differ for free (timestamps, randomness).

## What this deliberately does not change

- No close-safety or gate change: `apply-result.ts` and `unsafeCanonicalPullRequestReason` are untouched. The attestation sits beside the model verdict; nothing consumes it yet (that is scope 3 of the issue, maintainer-gated).
- No dashboard change, no new or changed labels (scope 2).
- No workflow yml: the lane only runs when invoked, and the subcommand itself is a no-op unless `CLAWSWEEPER_REPRODUCE_PROOF_ENABLED` is set, so activation stays an explicit maintainer decision.
- Raw reproduction output never reaches a record, a comment, a label, or a model prompt. Only exit codes, sha256 output hashes, byte counts, and durations are recorded.

## Security boundaries flagged for explicit maintainer review

Per VISION, changes touching untrusted execution and credentials need explicit review. The specific boundaries here:

1. Non-root execution. The sandbox is `sudo -n unshare --net` plus `setpriv`, and it never runs contributor code as root: when the lane runs as root the identity is mapped to an unprivileged uid and gid (65534), the checkout is chowned to that identity, and the probe (`sudo -n unshare --net -- setpriv ... -- sh -c '[ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]'`) fails the whole run to `netns_unavailable` unless the command actually executes as non-root. Passwordless sudo and setpriv on the Blacksmith runners are unproven; the worst case is a lane that only emits neutral records until the runner is provisioned.
2. The repro subprocess env is an allow-list built from scratch (`PATH`, `LANG`, plus `CI=true`), passed through `env -i` inside the sandbox so sudo's env handling cannot substitute it, and never a strip of `process.env`. This is deliberately stronger than `targetValidationEnv()`, which leaves `CLAWSWEEPER_PROOF_INSPECTION_TOKEN`, `CLAWSWEEPER_APP_*`, and crabfleet tokens in place. On top of that, every reproduction run (not only root-remapped ones) gets an isolated `HOME` and isolated `XDG_*`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`, `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`/`NPM_CONFIG_CACHE`, `CODEX_HOME`, and `GH_CONFIG_DIR` under a per-run directory, so untrusted code never reads the runner's real home or its credential-bearing dotfiles (`~/.npmrc`, `~/.gitconfig`, `~/.config/gh`, and so on). Tests assert the runner home never appears and none of the credential keys can appear.
3. Dependency install is a separate, additionally-gated boundary. By default the lane installs nothing: a PR whose reproduction needs unvendored dependencies fails identically on base and head and resolves to neutral, never reaching a registry. Install (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`, outside the network namespace because the registry needs network, with lifecycle scripts disabled) runs only when `CLAWSWEEPER_REPRODUCE_PROOF_ALLOW_SETUP=1` is set in addition to enabling the lane, so the network-touching step requires an explicit second maintainer opt-in.
4. The declared command is normalized through the existing allow-list (`parseAllowedValidationCommand`), which rejects shell one-liners, inline interpreter code, and non-allow-listed executables; rejection yields a neutral `command_unresolvable`, not a skip of the sandbox.

## Verification

- `pnpm run check` (build:all, oxlint, test:unit, test:repair, coverage, format:check) on Node 24.
- New tests: `test/reproduce-proof.test.ts` (sandbox argv, env allow-list purity, command allow-listing, verdict matrix, engine call-order and fail-closed paths via an injected exec), `test/proof-attestation.test.ts` (round-trip, reader recompute beats tampered verdicts, strict parser rejections, schema required-equals-properties invariant, marker and comment rendering), plus decision-parser and pr-proof-automation additions (reproCommand parse and round-trip, old reports default to null, eligibility matrix, candidate scan, flag default-off).
- Full `pnpm run check` passes end to end. One note for reproducibility: `test/sweep-workflow.test.ts` "apply workflow drops a coverage-proof tail only after exact trace examination" is flaky in this development environment when invoked standalone outside the check chain, and fails identically on pristine main `c089d676` there, so it is unrelated to this change.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: ClawSweeper trusts pasted proof it never re-runs; this adds a lane that reproduces a declared proof command on base vs head in a network-denied, credential-free, non-root sandbox and writes a head-pinned attestation, staying fail-closed neutral when the sandbox or the reproduction cannot be established.
Real environment tested: the real `dist/clawsweeper.js` CLI and the real reproduction engine on this Linux host, driving real `git`, real `sudo unshare --net`, real `setpriv` de-privileging to uid 65534, and real subprocesses against a two-commit repository whose base fails the declared command and whose head passes; compared against pristine main `c089d676` for the before side. Nothing was mocked.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node dist/clawsweeper.js reproduce-proof` (flag unset), then a driver that provisions a `/tmp` workspace like the lane and invokes `executeReproduceProof({repoDir, baseSha, headSha, command: resolveReproCommand("node check.mjs")})` followed by `writeProofAttestation` and `renderProofAttestationComment`, plus a direct sandbox invocation printing the in-sandbox uid and network state, and the same engine call with sudo removed from PATH.
Evidence after fix:

```
# BEFORE (pristine main c089d676): the lane does not exist
$ node dist/clawsweeper.js reproduce-proof
Unknown command: reproduce-proof

# AFTER (this patch): default-off flag makes the lane a no-op
$ node dist/clawsweeper.js reproduce-proof
[reproduce-proof] 2026-07-07T04:02:58.010Z disabled: set CLAWSWEEPER_REPRODUCE_PROOF_ENABLED=1 to enable this lane
[]

# AFTER (this patch): the sandbox runs as a non-root identity with no network (head commit)
$ sudo -n unshare --net -- setpriv --reuid=65534 --regid=65534 --clear-groups -- \
    env -i CI=true PATH=/opt/node24/bin:/usr/bin:/bin HOME=<checkout> sh -c 'echo "uid=$(id -u) gid=$(id -g)"; node check.mjs'
uid=65534 gid=65534
network: denied
OK: parseAmount("1,5") = 1.5

# AFTER (this patch): live reproduction as root -> mapped to unprivileged uid, base twice then head, attested
repro command: ["node","check.mjs"]
base 23818028a7e67c4b78c8ba20a88c3c7687c1b95a head 93e2b0c345c0e26613edf2a08f3c083056260e64
running as uid 0 -> engine maps root to unprivileged identity
  "before":  { "ref": "base", "exit": 1, "output_hash": "sha256:bb9d9409b75d53e472772864d7cd21a8801266ae7ea98ea3ed1149d985b2e59c", ... }
  "base_stability": { "second_exit": 1, "second_output_hash": "sha256:bb9d9409b75d...", "stable": true }
  "after":   { "ref": "head", "exit": 0, "output_hash": "sha256:f79d8a0a40873df292dcf292c58fda03f162c9569c520e9b7b1e66dcff7c8e38", ... }
  "differentiates": true,
  "verdict": "attested"
marker comment rendered beside the model verdict:
  Verdict: attested. The declared reproduction shows a stable behavior delta between base and head.
  Raw command output is withheld by policy; only exit codes, output hashes, and sizes are recorded.
  <!-- clawsweeper-proof-attestation item="421" sha="93e2b0c345c0e26613edf2a08f3c083056260e64" v="1" -->

# AFTER (this patch): fail-closed when the sandbox cannot be created (sudo absent from PATH)
verdict=neutral reason=netns_unavailable runs=none
```

Observed result after fix: on identical inputs the lane went from nonexistent to producing a head-pinned attested record for a real base-fail/head-pass delta through the real network-denied sandbox running as uid 65534, and to a neutral `netns_unavailable` record with zero runs when the sandbox could not be created.
What was not tested: the lane was not run against a live GitHub PR end to end (no comment was posted to a real PR), and `sudo`/`setpriv` availability on the Blacksmith runners was not verified; on runners without them every record is neutral by design.

Closes nothing on its own; this is scope 1 of https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/issues/421. Scope 2 (dashboard surface) and scope 3 (close-safety preferring a valid attestation, default-off) remain follow-ups gated on maintainer direction.
